summary: Master TVET management and industry partnership development. Build CBT curricula, MOU frameworks, and quality systems. Enrol today.
lede: Technical and vocational education management connects institutional priorities, training design and employer collaboration to workforce needs. For mid-career leaders and programme managers, this course covers assessing institutional performance, using labour-market and graduate-outcome information, and shaping competency-based curricula with industry input. Participants also practise structuring partnership agreements and planning employer engagement.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career professionals who manage, coordinate, or directly influence TVET institutional strategy, curriculum quality, and employer engagement. Whether you lead an institution, oversee a training programme, or manage the relationship between your organisation and industry partners, this course gives you the frameworks and tools to operate with greater precision and credibility.
audience: Skills Authority and TVET Regulatory Officers
Corporate Training Managers in large enterprises
National and Regional TVET Policy Advisors
modules: TVET Systems, Governance, and the Management Mandate
Labour Market Intelligence and Demand-Driven Programme Design
Competency-Based Training Curriculum Design with Industry
Industry Partnership Models and MOU Frameworks
TVET Quality Assurance and Accreditation Management
Industry Partnership Development Planning and Stakeholder Engagement
Institutional Strategy, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement
prerequisites: Participants should bring a laptop or tablet capable of running standard office productivity software (word processing and spreadsheet applications). Pre-configured exercise templates, the UNESCO-UNEVOC Balanced Scorecard instrument, tracer study templates, MOU draft frameworks, and the ISO 21001:2018-aligned audit checklist will be provided by the facilitator — no additional software licences are required. Participants are encouraged to bring institutional data (enrolment figures, completion rates, existing partnership agreements) to use as live inputs during workshop exercises, subject to any confidentiality constraints of their organisation.
